ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUNCN1BpOWJBEAE:
Hospital Review (Dental Treatment Experience)

After spending 5 hours in an appointment at this hospital, I decided to share my firsthand experience because over the past 5 years, there have been both positive and disappointing things.

Initially, the clinic I'd been going to since childhood recommended this hospital for root canal treatment. The first dentist who performed the root canal was excellent; the procedure was successful on the first try, and I was truly impressed. However, when I switched to another dentist for a crown, the tooth developed problems and eventually fell out. Fortunately, the second dentist admitted their mistake and sincerely apologized. The cost was over 50,000 baht for the first tooth (implant + denture).
Later, I had another tooth crowned. I remember the day of the procedure; the instruments made a loud "thud" that startled me. After returning home, simply biting into a mango caused the crown to break. I tried to book an appointment at the hospital, but they were fully booked, so I went to a clinic near my workplace, but that only provided a temporary solution.
After COVID-19 in 2022, I returned to this hospital hoping for a more permanent solution and chose a new dentist. However, problems persisted. This time, the dentist said the entire procedure needed to be removed and redone, initially stating they would not charge me. However, I was charged after the work was completed. Fortunately, I clearly remember the dentist saying there would be no charge that day. I argued with the cashier until they finally waived the lab fee, but they still charged me 5-6 thousand baht.

It felt like I jumped from the frying pan into the fire. I spent hundreds of thousands of baht but received service that was very disappointing.

Areas for improvement:
1. Accountability for expenses:
If it's a rework or correction due to a previous doctor's error, it should be settled within the hospital, not the burden shifted to the patient with the excuse of a different doctor.
2. Data recording system:
Estimates should be clearly recorded, such as using color coding on the bill or in the system, to prevent patients from wasting time arguing with cashiers.
3. Communication and service:
Some staff members spoke poorly and lacked empathy, even though the costs were comparable to private hospitals, yet the quality of service was lower.
4. Appointment system:
Difficult to contact, calls are often missed, and they don't call back even though they have patient information. This wastes patients' time and causes frustration.
5. Quality of treatment:
After the procedure, the teeth should be fully functional. The doctor said I could chew everything except tartar. But the truth is, even chewing crispy noodles can cause problems in less than 6 months.

Good things:
• All the doctors I met were kind and friendly. I can confirm they were Nice 👍
• They made an effort to take responsibility, although it wasn't perfect.

Conclusion:
I spent hundreds of thousands of baht but received service that was disproportionate to the price.
I also wasted time, suffered emotionally, and experienced mental health issues due to a substandard system.
If this were truly a specialized university hospital, it should be doing much better in terms of treatment quality, appointment system, after-sales service, and the attentiveness of its staff.
